transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I suppose it’s a little embarrassing to say, because I know it may sound minor. I have this scar on my wrist, and I do understand it’s probably not as bad as it looks to me. But when I’m at church, or playing bridge, I keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it… like it’s the first thing they notice about me now. I know that may not make much sense, but it’s been bothering me.
When you think about the scar, do you find yourself focusing on it a lot throughout the day, even when you're not around other people, or is it mostly a concern when you're in social situations?

It’s mostly when I’m around people, I think. I mean, I do notice it myself, of course, but it’s not as if I’m sitting home thinking about it every minute. It’s more when I’m at church or playing bridge… I start feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to my wrist, like it’s the first thing they see. I know it probably isn’t nearly as bad as it looks to me, but that’s how it feels.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations or activities because of worries about how others might see you or judge you, even when it’s not directly about the scar?

A little, yes… though I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely shutting myself away or anything. I’ve skipped a few choir things and some theater volunteer commitments because I get so worked up trying to make sure my wrist won’t be noticed. And, um… I’ve been late turning in some of my bookkeeping work too, because I spend too long fussing over how to cover it. I know that probably sounds silly.
Do these worries about your wrist ever cause you a lot of emotional distress, like anxiety or sadness, even when you’re not in the middle of a social situation?

I’m not sure I’d call it a lot, exactly… I mean, I don’t want to overstate it. If I’m just at home by myself, I can usually put it out of my mind. Sometimes I’ll feel a little uneasy or embarrassed if I happen to notice it, but it’s mostly when I’m thinking about being around people that it bothers me. Does that make sense?
When you’re in situations where your wrist might be visible, do you feel intense anxiety or a strong urge to leave, or do you try to avoid those moments altogether?

I don’t usually get to the point of, you know, running out of a room or anything dramatic like that. But I do get pretty wound up beforehand if I think my wrist might show. I’ll spend too long trying to cover it, and then I’ve ended up late with some bookkeeping work because of it.

And I have skipped a few choir things and theater volunteer commitments… not because I don’t want to go, really, just because I get so caught up in making sure no one will notice. I know that may sound a bit foolish.
Do these concerns about your scar ever interfere with your ability to do things you need to do or enjoy, even if it’s not about being around people?

Yes… I suppose it does, a bit. I don’t want to make it sound like it’s taking over my life, because it isn’t, but I have been late turning in some of my bookkeeping work because I get stuck trying to make sure my wrist is covered.

And I’ve skipped a few choir things and theater volunteer commitments too. I enjoy those, so it’s not that I don’t care about them… I just get so caught up worrying that someone might notice. I know that probably sounds like a lot for such a small thing.
Are there times when you feel anxious or worried about being judged by others, even in situations that don’t involve your wrist or how you look?

I don’t think so, not really. I mean, everyone worries a little about what people think, I suppose, but I haven’t noticed that being a problem for me in general. It’s more… tied to that one thing. If my wrist isn’t involved, I usually feel fairly normal around people. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you feel that the scar makes you look ugly or deformed, or is it more that you're worried others will judge you because of it?

I suppose it’s a little of both… though I know, rationally, the scar on my wrist probably isn’t as bad as it seems to me. I wouldn’t want to say I look deformed exactly, that sounds too strong.

But when I’m at church, or playing bridge, I do get this feeling that everyone’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice about me now. I know they may not actually be thinking that, but it feels that way. Is that what you mean?
When you’re not around other people, do you still find yourself frequently checking the scar or feeling that it looks much worse than it really is?

Yes… I do, though I wouldn’t say it’s constant. It’s mostly before I leave the house. I’ll look at my wrist in the hall mirror a few times, and then I might change sleeves or try a bracelet to make sure it’s covered.

Sometimes I ask my husband if it looks obvious, which is silly because he always says it’s barely there. I know I probably shouldn’t keep asking, but it just reassures me for a moment. Is that the sort of checking you mean?

When you look at the scar, do you see it as a noticeable defect that you believe others would find unappealing, or is it more about feeling that others might think negatively about you in general when they see it?

I think it’s more that the scar feels very noticeable to me… though I do know, logically, it probably isn’t as bad as I’m making it in my head.

When I’m at church or playing bridge, I get this uncomfortable sense that people’s eyes go right to my wrist, like it’s the first thing they notice now. I don’t know that they’d find it exactly unappealing, but I worry they’ll notice it and think something about it. Does that make sense?
Would you say your concern is specifically about how the scar looks, or is it more about how people might judge you overall when they see it?

I think it’s more specifically about how the scar looks… though I feel a bit silly saying that, because I do know it’s probably not nearly as noticeable as it seems to me.

But when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to my wrist, like it’s the first thing they notice about me now. I suppose I worry what they might think, too, but it starts with the way it looks to me. Does that answer it?
When you're worried about people noticing your scar, is your main concern about how the scar itself looks, or are you more worried that they'll think less of you as a person because of it?

I think it’s mostly about how the scar itself looks. I mean, I know it’s probably not as bad as it seems to me, and I don’t want to make too much of it… but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like people’s eyes go straight to my wrist, like it’s the first thing they notice now.

I suppose I do worry a little about what they might think, but it starts with the scar looking so obvious to me.
Is your concern mainly about the way the scar looks on your wrist, or do you worry more that people will judge you negatively as a person when they see it?

It’s mainly the way the scar looks on my wrist, I think. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is—I do know it’s probably not as bad as it looks to me.

But when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like people’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice about me now. I guess I worry a little what they’ll think, but mostly it’s that it seems so noticeable to me.
Do you feel self-conscious about the appearance of any other parts of your body, or is your main concern limited to the scar on your wrist?

No, not really other parts of my body. I mean, I have the usual things at my age I don’t love, but nothing I dwell on like this.

It’s mostly just the scar on my wrist. I know it’s probably not as bad as it looks to me, but when I’m at church or at bridge, I keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to it, like it’s the first thing they notice now. I hope that makes sense.
Do you believe that the scar appears much worse than others would objectively see it, or do you feel that even if it’s noticeable, the way others might react to it is what worries you most?

I think… more that it looks worse to me than it probably does to other people. I can tell myself it’s just a scar and maybe others don’t notice it much, but when I’m at church or playing bridge, I keep feeling like everyone’s eyes go right to my wrist.

It feels like it’s the first thing they see now, even though I know that may not be completely true. Does that answer what you mean?
